ettorescola.description: A screenwriter of Italian comedies who became their most reflective director.

facts.text: A Special Day takes place during Hitler's 1937 visit to Rome.
Le Bal tells fifty years of French history without dialogue.

idalupino.signature: The only woman directing in Hollywood in the 1950s.
idalupino.description: A star actress who formed her own company to make low-budget films on subjects the studios avoided.

facts.text: The Hitch-Hiker is regarded as the first American film noir directed by a woman.
Later directed many television episodes.

dorothyarzner.signature: The only woman director of the Hollywood studio era's first decades.
dorothyarzner.description: She rose from typist to editor to director at Paramount and made films about working women and female friendship.

facts.text: Was the first woman to join the Directors Guild of America.
Is credited with devising an early boom microphone.

johnfrankenheimer.signature: Paranoid thrillers shot with the urgency of live television.
johnfrankenheimer.description: He came from live TV drama and brought its deep-focus, wide-angle staging to political thrillers in the 1960s.

facts.text: Directed over a hundred live television dramas before his film career.
The Manchurian Candidate, Seven Days in May and Seconds are sometimes called his paranoia trilogy.

robertsiodmak.signature: The German émigré who made some of the darkest film noirs.
robertsiodmak.description: He began in Berlin, fled the Nazis and at Universal in the 1940s made shadowy thrillers of fate and betrayal.

facts.text: Co-directed People on Sunday in Berlin with Edgar G. Ulmer; Billy Wilder co-wrote it.
The Killers gave Burt Lancaster his first film role.

roubenmamoulian.signature: A stage innovator who freed the early sound camera.
roubenmamoulian.description: An Armenian-born Broadway director who experimented with moving cameras, layered sound and colour in early talkies.

facts.text: Becky Sharp was the first feature in three-strip Technicolor.
Directed the original Broadway productions of Porgy and Bess and Oklahoma!

alanclarke.signature: British television's fiercest realist, known for relentless walking shots.
alanclarke.description: He made confrontational dramas for the BBC about borstals, skinheads and Northern Ireland, often following characters with a Steadicam.

facts.text: Gus Van Sant named his Elephant after Clarke's 1989 film.

alanisobomsawin.signature: The leading documentarian of Indigenous life in Canada.
alanisobomsawin.description: An Abenaki filmmaker who has made dozens of films at the National Film Board about First Nations struggles.

facts.text: Spent 78 days behind the barricades filming the Oka crisis.

albertocavalcanti.signature: A cosmopolitan who linked the French avant-garde, British documentary and Ealing.
albertocavalcanti.description: A Brazilian who worked in Paris, then at the GPO Film Unit and Ealing Studios, where he pushed experiments with sound.

facts.text: Directed the ventriloquist episode of Dead of Night.

amyheckerling.signature: Sharp, affectionate comedies of American teenagers.
amyheckerling.description: Her high-school films defined teen slang and style for two different decades.
